title: Architecture in One Level
objective: After this level you can explain what architects do and how buildings changed over time.
summary: Vitruvius: good building needs firmness, commodity and delight. Architects design and draw what builders build, and building moved from mud brick and stone to iron, glass and steel.

cards.headline: The oldest surviving book on architecture says a building needs three things.
cards.body: The Roman architect Vitruvius wrote it about 2,000 years ago, and it's the only complete book on architecture to survive from ancient Greece and Rome. Architects still quote his list. Here it is, plus what architects actually do and how building changed.

cards.headline: Firmness, commodity, delight
cards.body: Vitruvius named three principles: firmitas, utilitas and venustas. A famous 1624 English version made them firmness, commodity and delight. Firmness means strength: it stands up. Commodity means it's useful to the people inside. Delight means it's beautiful. Miss one and the building fails: a gorgeous house with a leaky roof, or a sturdy box nobody can bear to look at. This chapter is all about the first one.

mascot.line: If you remember one thing from this level, make it these three words: firmness, commodity, delight.

cards.headline: The chief builder
cards.body: Architect comes from the Greek arkhitekton: arkhi-, chief, plus tekton, builder. Today an architect helps a client pin down what they need, designs the building, and produces drawings with technical specifications that builders can price and build from. They advise on approvals like planning permission, and they can inspect the work on site. An architect rarely lays a brick. The drawings say where every one goes.

cards.headline: How building changed, in six steps

events.label: Sun-dried mud brick, one of the first building materials
Posts and beams: stone laid across uprights
Rome's Pantheon rises under a great concrete dome
London's Crystal Palace: prefabricated iron and glass
Chicago's Home Insurance Building: an iron and steel skeleton

cards.headline: Architecture: mapped
learned: Architects design and hand builders drawings and specifications
From mud brick and stone to iron, glass and steel

questions.prompt: Vitruvius's three conditions for good building became which three words in a famous 1624 English version?

options.label: Stone, brick and wood
options.rationale: Those are building materials, not Vitruvius's principles.

options.label: Plan, section and elevation
options.rationale: Those are kinds of architectural drawing.

options.label: Posts, beams and arches
options.rationale: Those are ways of building, not his three conditions.

questions.explanation: Vitruvius named firmitas, utilitas and venustas; the 1624 English version made them firmness, commodity and delight.

questions.prompt: What does an architect mainly hand builders to work from?

options.label: The bricks and steel for the job
options.rationale: Builders supply materials; the architect supplies the design.

options.label: A finished building, built by the architect
options.rationale: Architects design and oversee; builders build.

options.label: A rough idea, for builders to design themselves
options.rationale: The design work is the architect's job.

questions.explanation: An architect designs the building and produces drawings with technical specifications that builders price and build from.

questions.prompt: On this chapter's timeline, which came between Rome's Pantheon and London's Crystal Palace?

options.label: The first sun-dried mud bricks
options.rationale: Mud brick is at least 6,000 years old, far earlier than both.

options.label: Chicago's Home Insurance Building
options.rationale: That came in 1884-85, after the Crystal Palace of 1851.

options.label: Nothing: they were built in the same year
options.rationale: They are more than 1,700 years apart.

questions.explanation: The Pantheon was rebuilt in 118-128 CE and the Crystal Palace opened in 1851; Florence's dome was built from 1420 to 1436, in between.
